column1: # param_presentation.tsv — PRESENTATION, keyed on ADDRESS and nothing else.
# WHY A SEPARATE TABLE. FOUNDATIONS' D1 ruling (their DECISIONS #89): ParamDesc
# carries STRUCTURE — address, id, type, cadence, ranges, and mod_min/mod_max —
# and deliberately does NOT carry label/unit/page/widget, because the standing
# GUI criterion says styling is data, separable from structure, and putting them
# in one record breaks the thing that criterion separates. Structure is theirs to
# define at re-point; presentation is ours, and lives here.
# KEYED ON ADDRESS, NEVER ON id. Their caution, adopted verbatim: a page or group
# that is also a dispatch fact is how the two get re-fused. gui.html today binds
# every control with data-p="<numeric id>" — that mistake is already in the tree,
# and this table is the shape meant to replace it. There is deliberately no id
# column: you cannot re-fuse what you cannot name.
# NO patch_scope COLUMN EITHER, and that is the same ruling applied to ourselves.
# Patch-scope is DISPATCH — does the write consume the event — not presentation
# and not location (their D2). It is derived from the shell by tools/gui_reach.py,
# with two semantic anchors that took three wrong versions to get right. Copying
# that derivation here to decorate a row would be a second copy of a rule whose
# single copy is the whole point. If you want to know whether a param is
# patch-scope, ask gui_reach; it is the owner.
# `chunk` IS THE QUEUE, AND EMPTY MEANS NOT-YET-DESIGNED.
# `shown_when` HIDES A ROW THAT CANNOT AFFECT THE SOUND. Grammar:
# `scale` = log10 MAPS THE CONTROL, NOT THE VALUE. Time is perceived
# logarithmically — 1->2 ms matters as much as 1->2 s — so a linear seconds
# slider spends most of its travel where nobody sets it. The GUI converts on
# send and on paint; the parameter itself stays linear seconds, which is what
# CLAP reports and what the core reads.
# A control for a parameter the engine does not read in the current mode is
# not information, it is furniture that lies. Every entry here is VERIFIED
# against the core's own branch (swarm_core.h topology switch), never
# inferred from a name: topo==0 reads poles, topo==1 reads reach, and the
# else branch (two-cluster) reads mu and balance.
# A row renders only when its chunk is named. This exists because the first pass
# generated a control for EVERY row at once to make gui_reach report 105/105 —
# a number, not a design. It surfaced SPECTRA and the engine selector into a GUI
# whose own rules say "a cluster appears here only when its engine surface is
# REAL", rendered every enum as a numeric slider, duplicated an existing panel,
# and shipped unstyled. Reach counted presence, so reach was satisfied.
# Naming a chunk is therefore a claim that four decisions were MADE for it:
#   1. engine surface is real (no cluster for an engine we are not shipping)
#   2. widget per param is right (an enum is a selector, not a number)
#   3. the group does not already exist hand-written (no twin panels)
#   4. the wrapper has CSS and survives at plugin size
# SEEDED, NOT INVENTED. Group and widget are mined from gui.html — the GUI that
# already reaches 102/105 params — so the starting data is what we ship, not a
